result.summary:
Implemented review-test-completion-r02.md exactly, bounded to the two areas it named: the room-ordinal loop's explicit typing, and a full rework of the appended reference-cross-check/non-aliasing block from the prior patch. Nothing else in the file was touched -- no existing refusal/fixture/matrix test, no oracle constant, and no production module was edited.

Hunk A: `for ordinal in range(1, 4):` in `test_room_ordinals_are_not_the_protected_room_type_ids` becomes `for ordinal: int in range(1, 4):` (explicit loop variable type), no other change to that function.

Hunk B: the entire block this candidate previously appended (from `# --- frozen layout-reference.json cross-check ...` through end of file, one large `_to_int_array` helper plus two long test methods) is replaced by a set of small, single-purpose, typed, and documented helpers and tests, each well under the 30-source-line limit:
- `DIAGRAM_ORACLE`: the exact eight frozen diagram rows, transcribed literally from layout-reference.json's own `diagram` array, per the instruction's 'simplest literal eight-row comparison' option.
- `_load_layout_reference()`: guards file existence, readability, and Dictionary parse; records a failure and returns `{}` on any miss, never continuing to index a bad result.
- `_typed_array(reference, key)`: guards key presence AND that the value is actually an Array before ever returning it for indexing; `{}`/missing/wrong-typed all fail loudly and return `[]`.
- `_int_or_fail(value, message)`: only accepts an `int` or an integral `float` (checked via `floor()` equality) before coercing; anything else fails and returns 0 rather than silently matching.
- `_int_array_guarded(values, message)`: maps every element through `_int_or_fail`.
- `test_frozen_layout_reference_diagram_matches_the_oracle`: compares all 8 loaded diagram rows (each individually type-checked as a String before `String()`-coercion) to DIAGRAM_ORACLE.
- `_assert_reference_furniture_row` + `test_frozen_layout_reference_furniture_matches_the_oracle`: guards every field key's presence on a Dictionary-typed row before any subscript, guards footprint/candidate_walk_tiles are Arrays before array-coercion, then compares against FURNITURE_ORACLE -- split so each function stays small.
- `_reference_edge_triples` + `test_frozen_layout_reference_edges_match_the_oracle`: guards every partition pair is an Array of length exactly 2 (and the door edge likewise) before ever indexing `[0]`/`[1]`, skipping (not crashing on) a malformed pair with a recorded failure, then compares the merged/sorted triples against all 8 EDGE_ORACLE rows.
- `_oracle_walk_tiles` + `test_frozen_layout_reference_exit_and_walk_tiles_match_the_oracle`: guards `exit_interior_tile` presence before subscripting; keeps the walk_tiles/reachable_walk_tiles-agree-with-each-other check, the 47-count check, and the independent 80-minus-footprints reconstruction check, all preserved from the prior patch.
- `_dirty_all_arrays(p, sentinel)`: the requested small typed helper that writes one sentinel into index 0 of all ten arrays, now used by `test_same_producer_two_outputs_do_not_alias` (functionally identical to before, just compact).

Every guard now actually prevents the unsafe indexing it precedes (returns/continues before any subscript on a shape it hasn't verified), rather than logging an assertion and proceeding regardless, closing the 'no tautological guards' finding. All new/changed loop variables carry explicit types. Every new function has a docstring.

CAVEAT (repeated from the prior turn, since the same constraint applies): I have no diff/patch tool and no file line numbers in this environment. I manually transcribed the exact old block from the full file content given in this dispatch (so every removed `-` line is character-for-character correct) and manually counted line offsets for the two `@@` headers; those counts may be off by a few lines even though I recounted them carefully against my own draft, since I can't execute anything to verify. The removed/added text itself is exact; a strict `git apply` may need the hunk header line numbers corrected first, which I cannot verify without execution. I have not run this diff or the resulting suite; no pass/fail claim is made, and the actual a4 run result is the one already supplied to me, not one I produced.

+# --- frozen layout-reference.json cross-check (review-test-followup-r01 item 1) ------------------
+
+const LAYOUT_REFERENCE_PATH: String = \
+	"res://../docs/validation/evidence/starter-integration-planning-2026-09-20/layout-reference.json"
+
+const FURNITURE_SYMBOL_KEY: Dictionary = {
+	"B": "bed", "K": "kitchen_bench", "H": "hearth", "T": "seat", "S": "shelf",
+}
+
+## The exact eight frozen diagram rows, transcribed literally from layout-reference.json.
+const DIAGRAM_ORACLE: Array = [
+	"BBBB..KKHH",
+	".........S",
+	"BBBB..TTTT",
+	"..........",
+	"BBBB..TTTT",
+	"......TTTT",
+	"..........",
+	"......SSSS",
+]
+
+
+func _load_layout_reference() -> Dictionary:
+	"""Load and guard the frozen JSON reference: existence, readability, Dictionary parse.
+	Returns an empty Dictionary, having recorded a failure, on any guard miss."""
+	if not FileAccess.file_exists(LAYOUT_REFERENCE_PATH):
+		fail("layout-reference.json must exist")
+		return {}
+	var raw: String = FileAccess.get_file_as_string(LAYOUT_REFERENCE_PATH)
+	if raw.is_empty():
+		fail("layout-reference.json must be readable")
+		return {}
+	var parsed: Variant = JSON.parse_string(raw)
+	if not (parsed is Dictionary):
+		fail("layout-reference.json must parse to a Dictionary")
+		return {}
+	return parsed
+
+
+func _typed_array(reference: Dictionary, key: String) -> Array:
+	"""The Array at `key`, guarded: key present and its value actually an Array. Empty, having
+	recorded a failure, otherwise -- never an unsafe subscript on a missing/wrong-typed key."""
+	if not reference.has(key):
+		fail("layout-reference.json must carry '%s'" % key)
+		return []
+	if not (reference[key] is Array):
+		fail("layout-reference.json's '%s' must be an Array" % key)
+		return []
+	return reference[key]
+
+
+func _int_or_fail(value: Variant, message: String) -> int:
+	"""An int coerced from an integral JSON number. Records a failure and returns 0 for any
+	non-numeric or fractional value, so a malformed element never silently coerces and matches."""
+	if value is int:
+		return value
+	if value is float and float(value) == floor(float(value)):
+		return int(value)
+	fail(message)
+	return 0
+
+
+func _int_array_guarded(values: Array, message: String) -> Array:
+	"""Every element of `values` coerced through _int_or_fail."""
+	var out: Array = []
+	for value: Variant in values:
+		out.append(_int_or_fail(value, message))
+	return out
+
+
+func test_frozen_layout_reference_diagram_matches_the_oracle() -> void:
+	"""The reference's own 'diagram' rows must equal the eight frozen literal oracle rows."""
+	var reference: Dictionary = _load_layout_reference()
+	var loaded: Array = _typed_array(reference, "diagram")
+	assert_equal(loaded.size(), DIAGRAM_ORACLE.size(), "diagram row count")
+	for row: int in range(mini(loaded.size(), DIAGRAM_ORACLE.size())):
+		if not (loaded[row] is String):
+			fail("diagram row %d must be a String" % row)
+			continue
+		assert_equal(String(loaded[row]), DIAGRAM_ORACLE[row], "diagram row %d" % row)
+
+
+func _assert_reference_furniture_row(loaded: Dictionary, expected: Dictionary, row: int) -> void:
+	"""One floor_furniture row, guarded: a Dictionary carrying every field this suite reads."""
+	for key: String in ["symbol", "origin", "room", "footprint", "candidate_walk_tiles"]:
+		if not loaded.has(key):
+			fail("reference furniture %d must carry '%s'" % [row, key])
+			return
+	var symbol: String = String(loaded["symbol"])
+	assert_true(FURNITURE_SYMBOL_KEY.has(symbol), "reference furniture %d has a known symbol" % row)
+	assert_equal(FURNITURE_SYMBOL_KEY.get(symbol, ""), expected["key"], "reference furniture %d key" % row)
+	assert_equal(_int_or_fail(loaded["origin"], "furniture %d origin" % row), int(expected["origin"]), "reference furniture %d origin" % row)
+	assert_equal(_int_or_fail(loaded["room"], "furniture %d room" % row), int(expected["room"]), "reference furniture %d room" % row)
+	if not (loaded["footprint"] is Array) or not (loaded["candidate_walk_tiles"] is Array):
+		fail("reference furniture %d footprint/candidates must be Arrays" % row)
+		return
+	assert_equal(_int_array_guarded(loaded["footprint"], "furniture %d footprint" % row), expected["footprint"], "reference furniture %d footprint" % row)
+	assert_equal(_int_array_guarded(loaded["candidate_walk_tiles"], "furniture %d candidates" % row), expected["candidates"], "reference furniture %d candidates" % row)
+
+
+func test_frozen_layout_reference_furniture_matches_the_oracle() -> void:
+	"""All 31 floor_furniture rows, guarded row-by-row, must equal FURNITURE_ORACLE."""
+	var reference: Dictionary = _load_layout_reference()
+	var loaded: Array = _typed_array(reference, "floor_furniture")
+	assert_equal(loaded.size(), FURNITURE_ORACLE.size(), "furniture entry count agrees with the reference")
+	for row: int in range(mini(loaded.size(), FURNITURE_ORACLE.size())):
+		if not (loaded[row] is Dictionary):
+			fail("reference furniture %d must be a Dictionary" % row)
+			continue
+		_assert_reference_furniture_row(loaded[row], FURNITURE_ORACLE[row], row)
+
+
+func _reference_edge_triples(reference: Dictionary) -> Array:
+	"""Every partition + the one door edge, guarded (length-2 pairs only) and merged into
+	[a, b, kind_key] triples sorted ascending by tile_a, mirroring EDGE_ORACLE's own order."""
+	var partitions: Array = _typed_array(reference, "solid_partition_edges")
+	var door: Array = _typed_array(reference, "door_edge")
+	var triples: Array = []
+	for pair: Variant in partitions:
+		if not (pair is Array) or pair.size() != 2:
+			fail("reference solid_partition_edges entry must be a length-2 pair")
+			continue
+		triples.append([_int_or_fail(pair[0], "edge tile_a"), _int_or_fail(pair[1], "edge tile_b"), "interior_partition"])
+	if door.size() == 2:
+		triples.append([_int_or_fail(door[0], "door tile_a"), _int_or_fail(door[1], "door tile_b"), "interior_door"])
+	else:
+		fail("reference door_edge must be a length-2 pair")
+	triples.sort_custom(func(a, b): return a[0] < b[0])
+	return triples
+
+
+func test_frozen_layout_reference_edges_match_the_oracle() -> void:
+	"""The reference's 7 partitions + 1 door, merged and sorted, must equal all 8 EDGE_ORACLE rows."""
+	var reference: Dictionary = _load_layout_reference()
+	var triples: Array = _reference_edge_triples(reference)
+	assert_equal(triples.size(), EDGE_ORACLE.size(), "partition + door edge count agrees with the reference")
+	for row: int in range(mini(triples.size(), EDGE_ORACLE.size())):
+		var loaded_edge: Array = triples[row]
+		var expected_edge: Dictionary = EDGE_ORACLE[row]
+		assert_equal(loaded_edge[0], expected_edge["a"], "reference edge %d tile_a" % row)
+		assert_equal(loaded_edge[1], expected_edge["b"], "reference edge %d tile_b" % row)
+		assert_equal(loaded_edge[2], expected_edge["kind"], "reference edge %d kind" % row)
+
+
+func _oracle_walk_tiles() -> Array:
+	"""The 80 interior tiles minus every FURNITURE_ORACLE footprint tile, ascending."""
+	var occupied: Dictionary = {}
+	for entry: Dictionary in FURNITURE_ORACLE:
+		for tile: int in entry["footprint"]:
+			occupied[tile] = true
+	var walk: Array = []
+	for local: int in 80:
+		if not occupied.has(local):
+			walk.append(local)
+	return walk
+
+
+func test_frozen_layout_reference_exit_and_walk_tiles_match_the_oracle() -> void:
+	"""The reference's exit_interior_tile and walk/reachable tile sets, guarded, against the
+	literal oracle and against this suite's own footprint-derived reconstruction."""
+	var reference: Dictionary = _load_layout_reference()
+	if reference.has("exit_interior_tile"):
+		assert_equal(_int_or_fail(reference["exit_interior_tile"], "exit_interior_tile"), EXIT_INTERIOR_LOCAL, "reference exit interior tile agrees with the literal oracle")
+	else:
+		fail("layout-reference.json must carry 'exit_interior_tile'")
+	var loaded_walk: Array = _int_array_guarded(_typed_array(reference, "walk_tiles"), "walk_tiles")
+	var loaded_reachable: Array = _int_array_guarded(_typed_array(reference, "reachable_walk_tiles"), "reachable_walk_tiles")
+	assert_equal(loaded_walk, loaded_reachable, "reference walk_tiles and reachable_walk_tiles agree with each other")
+	assert_equal(loaded_walk.size(), 47, "reference walk tile count matches the contract's 47")
+	assert_equal(loaded_walk, _oracle_walk_tiles(), "reference walk tiles equal 80 interior tiles minus this oracle's own footprints")
+
+
+# --- same-producer, two-output non-aliasing (review-test-followup-r01 item 2) ---------------------
+
+func _dirty_all_arrays(p: StarterStructures.Plan, sentinel: int) -> void:
+	"""Write `sentinel` into index 0 of every one of the ten arrays."""
+	p.buildings[0] = sentinel
+	p.rooms[0] = sentinel
+	p.room_tiles[0] = sentinel
+	p.furniture[0] = sentinel
+	p.footprints[0] = sentinel
+	p.candidate_access_tiles[0] = sentinel
+	p.edges[0] = sentinel
+	p.exit_tiles[0] = sentinel
+	p.bed_furniture_ordinals[0] = sentinel
+	p.header[0] = sentinel
+
+
+func test_same_producer_two_outputs_do_not_alias() -> void:
+	"""One producer, two outputs: mutating either must never mutate the other."""
+	var producer := StarterStructures.new()
+	var plan_a := StarterStructures.Plan.new()
+	var plan_b := StarterStructures.Plan.new()
+	assert_true(producer.prepare_into(plan_a), "first output prepares")
+	assert_true(producer.prepare_into(plan_b), "second output from the same producer prepares")
+	var snapshot_b := _snapshot_plan(plan_b)
+	_dirty_all_arrays(plan_a, 111)
+	_assert_plan_matches_snapshot(plan_b, snapshot_b, "mutating A must not alias B")
+
+	var snapshot_a := _snapshot_plan(plan_a)
+	_dirty_all_arrays(plan_b, 222)
+	_assert_plan_matches_snapshot(plan_a, snapshot_a, "mutating B must not alias A")
